answer: Because every new vertex in the trust graph requires fresh capital, an attacker running N fake agents pays N times the stake plus slashing risk, making mass identity creation economically irrational. Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a costly on-chain anchor: a deposit staked per identity at registration, slashed if the agent's quill signature ever appears on conflicting votes. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
